prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in such moire systems, without a claim on the pairing mechanism

statement.case_for: I keep B009 as my single-part configuration, and the round-1 exchange has sharpened rather than changed my reasons. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gave a quantitative, falsifiable condition for flat bands at a specific twist angle; the 2018 experiments from Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle; and the result has since been reproduced by many groups and carried to other moire platforms. The discovery can be stated in one sentence and rests on observed phenomena, not on any particular theory of them. Four of eight members now prefer it with identical names, and every member ranked it in the opening, but I rest my case on the physics, not the count. I would draft the citation around the flat bands and the observed states and say nothing about the pairing mechanism, so that later work on the mechanism cannot undermine the wording.
statement.case_against: The serious objection, pressed by Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson and Pearce, is that the interpretation is still moving: the pairing mechanism, the nature of several correlated phases, and the role of twist-angle disorder are unresolved eight years after the key experiments. A committee that values a prize which will not need revisiting could reasonably wait. The theory credit also has a visible neighbour in the earlier moire band-structure work of Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, and a three-name limit leaves out Cao as lead author, Dean, Young, Yacoby and others, which would draw criticism. Optical lattice clocks (B049) are more mature and more cleanly attributed, and I have not found a reason to think they are scientifically weak.

responses.point: Would let B009 mature longer because the origin of the superconductivity and the theory attribution are open, whereas lattice clocks have two decades of independent confirmation and no comparable interpretive question.
responses.response: I accept the premise that B049 is the more settled result, but I do not accept that the standard should be a settled mechanism. The flat bands at the predicted angle and the correlated and superconducting states are what has been reproduced, and these are observations that stand whatever the pairing turns out to be. Earlier prizes have honoured phenomena before their microscopic origin was understood. Your point on the theory attribution is the stronger one, and I answer it through the citation: the Bistritzer-MacDonald contribution is the quantitative magic-angle condition, which the earlier moire work did not give, so crediting that prediction does not deny the precursors. I would still concede that if the committee sets a mechanism-level bar, B009 fails it and B049 passes.

responses.point: Argues that the many-atom magic-wavelength scheme is a concept distinct from combs and ion control, that the credit is the cleanest on the list, and that waiting for the redefinition of the second would reward administrative timing.
responses.response: You have moved me on distinctness. In round 1 I treated lattice clocks as a refinement in the same lineage as 2005 and 2012, but your description of a new many-atom regime with its own polarizability and blackbody physics is a real concept, and Katori's idea and Ye's demonstration divide naturally. I also agree that the redefinition of the second should not decide whether the discovery is recognised, so I withdraw my suggestion that B049 can wait for it. What remains between us is whether a measurement-precision advance with null fundamental tests outweighs a new class of quantum matter, and on that I still come down on the side of B009. I acknowledge, as you do for your own field, that my judgement here is made from outside atomic physics, which is why I keep B049 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Rates B009 as a very strong candidate that gains from waiting, notes that Eriksson and Mehlig concede the interpretation is still moving, and moved to B049 because it has no comparable open interpretive question.
responses.response: I agree that your reasoning on B026 was sound and that the missing Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is a real obstacle, so I have moved B026 to second alternative and not a competitor. On B009, I read the concession by Eriksson and Mehlig differently: they say the mechanism is open, but they separate it from the discovery, as I do. I would turn your question around. If the committee waits for B009 on maturity and also for B049 on novelty, we may end up applying a stricter test to the candidate with the stronger new physics. I propose we apply one test to both, namely whether the discovery as worded is established, and check each citation against it.

responses.point: Would settle credit by the discovery narrative of flat-band prediction then correlated phases, keeping the citation on the platform and observed phases and not on the pairing debate.
responses.response: I agree, and I have adopted your approach in my citation. I would add one safeguard that follows from the Kroll and Johansson objections. The citation should name the theory contribution as the prediction of flat bands at a magic angle and not as the whole moire band structure, so that it does not overstate priority against Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto. On the experimental side, I think the credit to Jarillo-Herrero rests on the 2018 observation at the predicted angle, and that this is a defensible three-name boundary even though Dean and others contributed to the broader field.

responses.point: Moves B009 to first place, argues it is easy to state, falsifiable and reproduced, and keeps B049 and B011 as alternatives.
responses.response: I am glad we now agree on the lead, and I share your view that a quantitative prediction later confirmed is the pattern the prize is meant to reward. I would be more cautious than you on how far the argument can go, because saying a Nobel discovery does not need a settled mechanism is correct only if the citation is limited to the established findings. I would also note that your alternative B011 still has no support from others and the Tu omission remains unanswered, so I do not see it entering a final configuration.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will apply a mechanism-level maturity bar to B009, which it would fail, or a discovery-level bar, which it passes, and whether the same bar is being applied to B049.

Whether the experimental credit should rest on Jarillo-Herrero alone, given the roles of Cao as lead author and of Dean, Young and Yacoby, and whether the earlier moire work of Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto weakens the theory credit.

Whether B049 is better regarded as a new regime of measurement or as a refinement of the 2005 and 2012 lineage; I have been persuaded it is more than a refinement but remain unsure that it is a discovery in the sense the statutes use.
I judge both condensed-matter and atomic candidates from a high-energy-theory background and rely on the supplied record, which I have not independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. No specific conflict is apparent from my profile: none of the credited names for B009, B049 or B026 is among my documented connections (Gross, Rubinstein, Van Riet, the Uppsala theory group). My own field is high-energy theory and cosmology, so I am assessing these candidates from outside my specialty. I note the disclosures by Johansson (B040) and Kroll (B049) and take no position on whether they require recusal.
